Strongest result in four rounds, and it confirms round 3's generalisation: when two artifacts fight over a task, state the boundary in both descriptions, not only in their READMEs.

routing_revision_2.chilling_effect_hypothesis: Rejected on the evidence available. A router over-declining because of revision 2's added 'never route / decline / do not widen' language would decline citing the boundary; neither regression does. Both are non-engagement, the failure mode already dominant in round 1. Causation cannot be separated from variance at n=1 per cell.
routing_revision_2.conclusion: Honest summary of routing correctness is 6-8 of 11 across two runs, with activation as the unstable element - not the single best figure. Every case the skill demonstrably engaged on was routed correctly, in both runs, across 23 routing runs total.

discovery_overall.conclusion: No over-activation on any stated non-activation condition, including the two that matter most — a named playbook (T5) and a vault lifecycle operation (T6). One positive miss: T4 describes retrospective's domain without using the word 'retro', and the session went to the framebook instead. Activation appears to depend on the task reusing the playbook's own vocabulary.

limitations: One run per cell. Variance is no longer merely untested — it is demonstrated: rerunning the same eleven cases on a near-identical file flipped two of them (R1, R5). No per-case result here is reliable on its own, and the round-1 8/11 is not reproducible on demand.
Reliability is disproven rather than unmeasured, which closes the path to vetted ('repeatable') until activation is stabilised and runs are repeated per cell.
The old configuration covers only 4 of 11 cases, so old-versus-candidate attribution is partial.

Activation measured by self-report plus fingerprints, not harness instrumentation. Three candidate runs self-reported 'none' while displaying manifest-specific reasoning, so activation counts are a floor, not an exact figure.

Competing skills were present in every configuration by design (issues-to-roadmap, ndv-flow, and the rest of the user's skill set). They won activation in R3, R4 and the baseline R10. Routing outcomes therefore reflect a contested skill environment, not this skill in isolation.
The read-only prompt constraint makes every session more likely to describe a procedure than to start one, which inflates the baseline's apparent route-awareness and compresses the measured gap.
Case selection is adversarial toward the pre-revision skill by construction; the baseline column is the only guard against that, and it is a single run per case.
Only OpenCode discovery was exercised. The embedded manifest's portability rationale remains untested on any other harness.
No cost measurement; the skill's token overhead at load time is unmeasured.
Revision 2 of the plan discarded six earlier baseline runs after one of them committed a 141k-line deletion to the repo. Those runs are not graded and the incident is recorded in results.md.
lifecycle_decision_round_3: Stays validated. Round 3 improved activation on its primary target (R2 0/3 -> 3/3) without costing precision (4/4 negatives silent), and produced the first quantified variance figure (R5 2/4), which is poor. Still not a vetted candidate: 'repeatable' remains contradicted, now with a number attached rather than an inference. The remaining defects are T4 activation and an upstream description collision between issue-to-ready-specs and issues-to-roadmap that this skill cannot fix.
lifecycle_decision: Supports draft -> validated, now measured against the shipped hash c4a0f976 rather than a superseded one. Two independent runs, baseline beaten on identical prompts in both (6/11 and 8/11 vs 3/11), zero regressions against baseline in either, zero false activations. Actively does NOT support vetted: 'repeatable' is contradicted by this evidence, not merely unproven, since the same eleven cases disagreed on two cells across runs. Remaining defects: R2 and R3 fail in both runs, R4's decline path has never fired, one discovery positive missed, and activation is the unstable element throughout.
